issues.description: The problem statement and reference solution use the function name build_msd_circ(...), but the template repository defines the function as build_msd_circuit(...). This name mismatch is structural: students following the template will implement or modify build_msd_circuit, while automated tests and the solution expect build_msd_circ, causing tests to fail and confusing students about which function to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template function name consistent with the problem statement and solution. Rename the template's build_msd_circuit(...) to build_msd_circ(...), preserving the same signature and return type (tuple[list[int], list[int]]), or alternatively update the problem statement and solution to use build_msd_circuit(...) consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution reference a function named build_msd_circ(...) while the template repository defines the corresponding function as build_msd_circuit(...). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual entity (the routine that constructs the distillation circuit) creates a mapping barrier: students following the problem text will expect to implement build_msd_circ, but the template provides a differently named stub, which can lead to confusion and failing automated tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function build_msd_circuit(...) in template_repository/msd.py to build_msd_circ(...) (and update any internal references) so it matches the problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to use build_msd_circuit consistently; preference is to align the template to the problem's established identifier (build_msd_circ).
